messages.subject: A poisson model error
parts:
Hi, guys,

I saw a multivariate Poisson model from this paper http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0001457507001996

If my understanding is correct, the model should be like this:
y[i,j] ~ Poisson(x[i] * Beta[j] + Eta[i,j])  //i is the observation number, j is the categorical number
Eta[i] ~ Multi_normal(0, Omega)

I wrote the codes in Stan.

Multivariate Poisson model:

library(rstan)
users<-read.csv("Data1.CSV")
d<-users
d$constant<-1

model="
data{
int<lower=1> n;
int<lower=1> t; #t groups
int<lower=1> k; #k predictors
vector[n]  x1;
vector[n]  x2;
vector[n]  x3;
vector[n]  x4;
vector[n]  x5;
vector[n]  x6;
vector[n]  x7;
vector[n]  x8;
int<lower=0> y1[n];
int<lower=0> y2[n];
int<lower=0> y3[n];
cov_matrix[t]  sigma;
}

parameters{
matrix[t,k] Beta;
cov_matrix[t] w;
vector[t] Eta[n];
vector[t] mu;
}

model{
 for(i in 1:n) {
   y1[i]~poisson(exp(x1[i]*Beta[1,1]+x2[i]*Beta[1,2]+x3[i]*Beta[1,3]+x4[i]*Beta[1,4]+x5[i]*Beta[1,5]+x6[i]*Beta[1,6]+x7[i]*Beta[1,7]+x8[i]*Beta[1,8]+Eta[i,1]));
   y2[i]~poisson(exp(x1[i]*Beta[2,1]+x2[i]*Beta[2,2]+x3[i]*Beta[2,3]+x4[i]*Beta[2,4]+x5[i]*Beta[2,5]+x6[i]*Beta[2,6]+x7[i]*Beta[2,7]+x8[i]*Beta[2,8]+Eta[i,2]));
   y3[i]~poisson(exp(x1[i]*Beta[3,1]+x2[i]*Beta[3,2]+x3[i]*Beta[3,3]+x4[i]*Beta[3,4]+x5[i]*Beta[3,5]+x6[i]*Beta[3,6]+x7[i]*Beta[3,7]+x8[i]*Beta[3,8]+Eta[i,3]));
}

for(i in 1:t){
for(j in 1:k){
Beta[i,j]~normal(0,100);
}
}
for(i in 1:n){
Eta[i]~multi_normal(mu,w);
}
w~inv_wishart(t+1,sigma);
}"

muhat<-rep(0,3)
Imat<-diag(1,3)
d1<-list(n=nrow(d),k=8,t=3,mu=muhat,sigma=Imat,y1=d[,1],y2=d[,2],y3=d[,3],x1=d[,4],x2=d[,5],x3=d[,6],x4=d[,7],x5=d[,8],x6=d[,9],x7=d[,10],x8=d[,11])
m<- stan_model(model_code=model)
r<- sampling(m,data=d1)

Although this program can operates. However, it always shows these errors: 
Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:
stan::prob::multi_normal_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Covariance matrix is not symmetric. Covariance matrix[1,2] is -1.#IND:0, but Covariance matrix[2,1] element is -1.#IND:0.If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified.

And, the n_eff is only 2 for most parameters. I want to know:
1) How to get a symmetric covariance matrix in stan?
2) How to improve the covariance matrix to get larger n_eff?

Thanks

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] A poisson model error
parts:
You'll find everything much more stable arithmetially working
with a Cholesky factor of the covariance matrix. We actually
recommend scaling a correlation matrix --- see the discussion in
the regression chapter of the manual.

Also, you want to replace those poisson(exp(...)) with
poisson_log(...) --- we have a version parameterized on
the log scale and it's both more efficient and more arithmetically
stable.

I'd also recommend replacing all that long form dot product stuff
with matrix operations and using the vectorized version of poisson_log.
It'll be a lot faster and a lot easier to read.

- Bob

Hmmm, maybe there’s some nonidentifiability here?

Some quick comments:
- best to make y a 2-way array, then you can loop the model rather than having to repeat code 5 times everywhere.

It’s hard for me to follow your model in part because I get confused with arrays of vectors such as you have.  That’s my problem in that I’m not such a Stan expert.  I guess my suggestion to you is to first get things working with a single y (that is, just y1).  Then when that works go on to include all 5.  It’s hard for me to follow your model but I’m guessing there’s something that’s not really identified.

Also I’d try the noncentered parameterization:  instead of

y ~ poisson_log(x*Beta + Eta);
Eta~multi_normal(mu,diag_pre_multiply(sigma_beta,L_Omega));

Do something like:

y ~ poisson_log(x*Beta + mu + sigma_beta*Eta);
Eta ~ multi_normal(0, L_Omega);

Hmmm, maybe there’s some nonidentifiability here?

Some quick comments:
- best to make y a 2-way array, then you can loop the model rather than having to repeat code 5 times everywhere.
- maybe you can just make eta into a matrix; the way you’re doing the transpose is ugly.  It won’t be slowing down your program but this sort of thing looks like an invitation for bugs to crawl in.

It’s hard for me to follow your model in part because I get confused with arrays of vectors such as you have.  That’s my problem in that I’m not such a Stan expert.  I guess my suggestion to you is to first get things working with a single y (that is, just y1).  Then when that works go on to include all 5.  It’s hard for me to follow your model but I’m guessing there’s something that’s not really identified.

Also I’d try the noncentered parameterization:  instead of

y ~ poisson_log(x*Beta + Eta);
Eta~multi_normal(mu,diag_pre_multiply(sigma_beta,L_Omega));

Do something like:

y ~ poisson_log(x*Beta + mu + sigma_beta*Eta);
Eta ~ multi_normal(0, L_Omega);

Or something like that.  Again, I could be botching the multivariate stuff but that’s the general point.  Also, if x[1] is a constant term, you’ll be having nonidentifiability of beta[1] and mu.
